userStories.title: Persisted repo-scoped fix type and reset invariant
acceptanceCriteria: Given a PRD story with one `PersistedRepoScopedFix`, when `savePRD` then `loadPRD` run on the same path, then the loaded story's `repoScopedFixes` deep-equals the written array.
Given a prd.json whose stories omit `repoScopedFixes`, when `loadPRD` reads it, then each story's `repoScopedFixes` is `undefined`.
Given failed stories with `repoScopedFixes`, when `resetFailedStoriesToPending(prd, { resetRef: true })` runs, then every reset story has `repoScopedFixes` set to `undefined`.

Given failed stories with `repoScopedFixes`, when `resetFailedStoriesToPending(prd, { storyIsolation: "worktree" })` runs with default `resetRef`, then every reset story has `repoScopedFixes` set to `undefined`.
Given a failed story with `repoScopedFixes`, when `resetFailedStoriesToPending(prd, {})` runs, then the story retains its existing `repoScopedFixes`.
Given a passed story with `repoScopedFixes`, when `resetFailedStoriesToPending(prd, { resetRef: true })` runs, then the passed story retains its existing `repoScopedFixes`.

routing.reasoning: This is a focused additive type, barrel, loader-round-trip, and reset-path update across two source modules and existing unit suites.

userStories.title: Record repo-scoped dispatches on the executing story
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Map each resolved repo-scoped dispatch record onto the live story before the existing persistence paths run.

**Motivation** — Every #1660 carrier needs it on disk: `nax finish` is a separate phase that assembles PR context purely from on-disk artifacts, so the PR-body option is unreachable while records remain in memory.

**Approach** — Write to `ctx.story`, never `ctx.prd`. In parallel mode `buildWorktreePipelineContext` (`parallel-worker.ts:26-30`) deep-clones `prd` via `structuredClone` while passing `story` by reference, so a mutation of `ctx.prd` is discarded and a mutation of `ctx.story` is not. This is the same asymmetry `parallel-worker.ts:61` already depends on for `storyGitRef`.

The existing saves that carry the write:

| Path | Save point |
|:---|:---|
| Sequential, story passed | `completionStage` → `savePRD(ctx.prd, prdPath)` (`stages/completion.ts:200-202`), which runs immediately after `executionStage` in `defaultPipeline` (`stages/index.ts:32-41`) |
| Sequential, story failed | `handlePipelineFailure` → `markStoryFailed` + `savePRD` (`pipeline-result-handler.ts:337`, `:371`) |
| Parallel worktree | `reconcileBatchOutcome(prd, batchResult)` + `savePRD(prd, ctx.prdPath)` (`unified-executor.ts:383-384`) — worktree pipelines set `skipPrdPersistence`, so the executor is the single writer |

**Scope** — In: add the synchronous mapper, append mapped entries without `declinedReason`, re-export it through both execution barrels, inject it through `_executionDeps`, and call it after successful `plan.run()` resolution before inspection. Out: US-001's persisted type and reset changes; cross-process or cross-worker synchronisation; narrowing the crash window with a new save; commit annotation; PR-body rendering; repair caps; and fixing `outputFiles`/`diffSummary` persistence.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function recordRepoScopedFixes(
  story: UserStory,
  records: readonly RepoScopedFixRecord[] | undefined,
): void
```

`repo-scoped-fix-record.ts` imports `UserStory` and `PersistedRepoScopedFix` from the `@/prd` barrel (never a leaf path — `project-conventions.md` § Module Structure), and is re-exported from `src/execution/story-orchestrator/index.ts` and `src/execution/index.ts` alongside the existing `RepoScopedFixRecord` export.

`_executionDeps` gains a `recordRepoScopedFixes` key; `executionStage.execute` calls `_executionDeps.recordRepoScopedFixes(ctx.story, planResult.repoScopedFixes)` after the `try`/`catch`/`finally` around `plan.run()` and before `applyPostRunInspection`.

**Failure handling** — An absent or empty `records` argument is a no-op: `story.repoScopedFixes` is left untouched, and an empty array is never written. The recorder is synchronous and returns `void`, performs no awaited persistence, and relies entirely on existing saves. If `plan.run()` throws, no result is recorded and the existing rethrow is unchanged. A failed story retains records because its worktree and commits remain.

**Design boundary** — Do not reuse `RepoScopedFixRecord` for the disk type: `src/prd` imports nothing from `src/execution`, and the mapper deliberately copies only `triggeringTests`, `filesChanged`, and `findingsCleared` in source order.
acceptanceCriteria: Given one `RepoScopedFixRecord`, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, records)` runs, then `story.repoScopedFixes` deep-equals one entry containing the record's `triggeringTests`, `filesChanged`, and `findingsCleared`.

Given a `RepoScopedFixRecord` with `declinedReason: "gave up"`, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, records)` runs, then its persisted entry has exactly `triggeringTests`, `filesChanged`, and `findingsCleared` keys.
Given two source records, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, records)` runs, then `story.repoScopedFixes` contains two mapped entries in the source order.

Given a story with one persisted entry and one new source record, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, records)` runs, then `story.repoScopedFixes` contains the existing entry followed by the mapped new entry.
Given a story without `repoScopedFixes`, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, [])` runs, then `story.repoScopedFixes` remains `undefined`.
Given a story without `repoScopedFixes`, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, undefined)` runs, then `story.repoScopedFixes` remains `undefined`.
When `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, records)` is called, then it returns `undefined` rather than a Promise.
When `recordRepoScopedFixes` is imported from `@/execution`, then `typeof recordRepoScopedFixes` is `"function"`.

Given `executionStage.execute(ctx)` with a plan resolving a one-element `repoScopedFixes` array and a spy replacing `_executionDeps.recordRepoScopedFixes`, when the stage runs, then the spy is called exactly once with `ctx.story` and that same records array.

Given spies for `_executionDeps.recordRepoScopedFixes` and `_executionDeps.applyPostRunInspection`, when `executionStage.execute(ctx)` runs with plan records, then `recordRepoScopedFixes` is invoked before `applyPostRunInspection`.
Given `executionStage.execute(ctx)` with a plan result that has no `repoScopedFixes`, when the stage returns, then `ctx.story.repoScopedFixes` is `undefined`.
Given `executionStage.execute(ctx)` with `success: false` and one repo-scoped record, when the stage returns, then `ctx.story.repoScopedFixes` has length 1.
Given `executionStage.execute(ctx)` with a plan whose `run()` rejects with an error, when the stage is awaited, then it rejects with that same error.
Given `executionStage.execute(ctx)` with a plan whose `run()` rejects, when the stage rejects, then `ctx.story.repoScopedFixes` is `undefined`.
Given a story with an existing persisted entry, when `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, [])` or `recordRepoScopedFixes(story, undefined)` runs, then the existing entry remains unchanged.
Given a rejecting `plan.run()` and a spy replacing `_executionDeps.recordRepoScopedFixes`, when `executionStage.execute(ctx)` rejects, then the recorder spy has not been called.

routing.reasoning: This is a contained multi-module integration using established mutable dependency and barrel-export patterns, with ordering and failure-path behavior but no new persistence subsystem.

outOfScope: Cross-process or cross-worker synchronisation of the write — each story object is mutated by exactly one worker, so no locking is specified.
Narrowing the crash window between the write and the next `savePRD` — no new save point is added.

analysis:
The feature extends existing PRD and execution seams rather than creating persistence infrastructure. `UserStory` currently ends with the optional `storyGitRef` field at `src/prd/types.ts:233`; `src/prd/index.ts:10-22` is the public PRD barrel, and `loadPRD` reads JSON and normalizes only a fixed list of fields at `src/prd/index.ts:53-103`, so an optional unknown field round-trips without a migration or default. `savePRD` serializes the PRD at `src/prd/index.ts:106-109`. `resetFailedStoriesToPending` mutates only failed stories and already clears `storyGitRef` when `resetRef` is true or `storyIsolation === "worktree"` at `src/prd/index.ts:319-345`; `repoScopedFixes` must follow this exact reset condition so metadata never outlives the commits it describes. Existing focused coverage is in `test/unit/prd/prd-reset-failed.test.ts:113-136`, while the loader normalization/round-trip suite is `test/unit/prd/prd-auto-default.test.ts:32-299`.

The in-memory producer is `RepoScopedFixRecord` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/repo-scoped-fix-record.ts:22-59`; `deriveRepoScopedFixes` builds ordered records at `:62-94`, including the deliberately non-persisted `declinedReason`. The new mapper belongs in this leaf module and must import its PRD types from the `@/prd` barrel to preserve the execution-to-PRD dependency boundary. The story-orchestrator barrel presently exports the producer at `src/execution/story-orchestrator/index.ts:31-32`, and the execution barrel mirrors those symbols at `src/execution/index.ts:70-95`, so both must re-export the new recorder.

`executionStage.execute` obtains `planResult` after `plan.run()` in `src/pipeline/stages/execution.ts:156-181`, catches and rethrows run failures, unsubscribes in `finally`, then invokes `applyPostRunInspection`. Its mutable `_executionDeps` object at `:184-194` is the test seam. Recording must occur after a successful `plan.run()` resolution and before inspection; this retains records when `success` is false, avoids recording when `plan.run()` rejects, stays synchronous/fail-open, and leaves existing error propagation unchanged. `test/unit/pipeline/stages/execution-phase-telemetry.test.ts:69-90` demonstrates snapshotting and restoring `_executionDeps` around injected plan and inspection dependencies.

Parallel behavior is safe only if the mutation targets `ctx.story`: `buildWorktreePipelineContext` deep-clones `base.prd` at `src/execution/parallel-worker.ts:25-30`, while the live story reference is used to set `storyGitRef` at `:51-62`. Mutating `ctx.prd` would be discarded in the worktree path. Existing sequential completion/failure and parallel reconciliation saves therefore carry the live-story mutation; do not add a separate persistence call or alter commit paths. Compatibility is additive: old PRDs retain `undefined`, empty record input must not introduce `[]`, and no backfill or schema migration is required. Main risks are accidentally persisting `declinedReason`, replacing rather than appending retries, recording after the inspect/save boundary, or clearing records in shared mode where `storyGitRef` is intentionally retained.
outOfScope: Adding a git trailer, a git note, or an amended commit message to a story's commits is deferred to issue #1660.
Rendering repo-scoped fix records in the PR body composed by `src/finish/pr/body.ts` is deferred to a follow-up spec.
The `declinedReason` field of `RepoScopedFixRecord` is deliberately not persisted and stays only in the JSONL run log.
Fixing the pre-existing loss of `outputFiles` and `diffSummary`, which `handlePipelineSuccess` writes without a following `savePRD`, belongs to its own issue.
No cap is placed on the number of persisted entries per story; growth is bounded by `execution.rectification.maxAttemptsTotal` and is not managed here.
Backfilling `repoScopedFixes` onto PRDs from runs that completed before this feature is not attempted.
Persisting records for stories that never reach the execution stage — skipped, blocked, or queue-aborted — is not attempted.
US-002 only: cross-process or cross-worker synchronisation of `repoScopedFixes` writes is out of scope, because each story object is written by exactly one worker.
US-002 only: records written after the last `savePRD` of a run that then crashes are lost; no new save point is added to narrow that window.
